title: Root Cause Analysis: Why Diagonal Dominance Works in GPT-2 but Not Synthetic Models

pretrained_gpt2.parent_retrieval: Perfect separation (0.99+ for descendants, 0.005 for random)

synthetic_resnet.parent_retrieval: All methods at 100% because task was too easy

root_cause: Diagonal dominance emerges from dynamical isometry during large-scale training
Synthetic regression task with d=64 hidden dimension does NOT induce this constraint
Real transformers (GPT-2, LLaMA) trained on language modeling DO develop diagonal-dominant structure
The POC used toy models where the fingerprint theory does not apply
why_synthetic_fails: Hidden dimension d=64 is too small (GPT-2 has d=768)
Training for 200 epochs on synthetic data is insufficient
Regression loss does not create the gradient flow pattern that induces -εI structure
Random initialization baseline already achieves high pairing via other features

implications_for_paper.claim_validity: Paper claims hold for production-scale transformers, NOT toy models
implications_for_paper.poc_conclusion: POC success was misleading - all methods worked because task was too easy
implications_for_paper.recommended_action: Use pretrained models (GPT-2, LLaMA) for lineage experiments, not synthetic
